target_customer: Mobile players, especially teens and young adults, who want a social avatar world and creators
problem: People wanted a persistent social virtual world on mobile with user-created content.
business_model: Free-to-play with in-app purchases (assumed from category; not sourced)
product_category: Mobile social virtual world and gaming (Highrise)

founders.name: Anton Bernstein
founders.background_notes: Ran product and marketing at LuxuryEscapes.com per YC page.

founders.name: Jimmy Xu
founders.background_notes: YC page: nine years working on mainstream virtual worlds.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time 3D avatar world on mobile with creator tools is standard game engineering with hard scaling parts; no detailed source.

defensibility.rationale: Community and avatar creations create switching costs; not directly sourced.

market_need_then: Highrise launched in beta on iOS in March 2015 and Android in January 2020; the company later reports 50 million users.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand source read besides names of products (Highrise, Everskies).

outcome_analysis: Pocket Worlds, a Summer 2018 company, kept running Highrise, which Wikipedia says reached 50 million registered users by 2025, and grew by acquisitions (Everskies in 2021, Infinite Canvas in January 2025, Hotel Hideaway in September 2026 per the YC page). Funding evidence is thin: a $7M Series A led by Bitkraft in January 2021 appears only in a Wikipedia citation headline, so it is single-sourced and treated cautiously.
